warnings.message: LinkedIn profile https://www.linkedin.com/in/vaidees was blocked with HTTP 999. The LinkedIn certifications section is the most common location where candidates self-report professional certifications (Dell Proven Professional, AWS, Azure, VMware, Google Cloud, etc.). None of these are captured in this artifact. This is an unknown gap, not a confirmed absence. A human reviewer with authenticated LinkedIn access should inspect this profile.

Microsoft Learn transcript at learn.microsoft.com/en-us/users/vaideeswaranganesan/transcript/share returned a generic profile shell with no data. The username slug 'vaideeswaranganesan' was derived from the canonical name and may not match the candidate's actual Learn username. Any Microsoft certifications (AZ-900, AZ-104, AZ-305, MS-*, AI-900, etc.) stored on Microsoft Learn are NOT captured. Status is UNKNOWN.

GitHub profile https://github.com/vaideesg returned an access-restricted response. Credential metadata is not typically hosted on GitHub public profiles, but any README badges, pinned credential links, or GitHub Achievements are not captured. Gap noted.

All 3 discovered and captured credentials are participation badges (hackathon_participation category), not exam-based professional certifications. They signal collaboration, innovation, and hackathon engagement but do not attest to passing a formal examination or meeting a competency standard.

The Microsoft Garage (issuer_org_id_credly: 1f6cafc3-1e39-4782-908c-5b254ce0fdf0) has issuer_verified_on_credly=false as returned by the Credly API. This means Credly has not independently verified The Microsoft Garage as an organization. However, The Microsoft Garage is a well-known publicly documented Microsoft-internal innovation initiative; the unverified flag is an artifact of Credly's verification tier system, not evidence of a fraudulent issuer.

The Microsoft Garage is an internal Microsoft program. All three badges were issued by this entity. The candidate profile lists Dell as employer with no start or end dates. The temporal relationship between these hackathon participations (2022, 2023, 2025) and any Dell tenure is unresolvable from available data. This does not affect badge authenticity but is relevant to employment narrative context.
